annotations.text: We combine repeated evaluations, controlled task variations, and lifecycle interventions to examine whether improvements from skill evolution persist and transfer, and to trace their origins to feedback, revision, selection, skill content, and evaluation.
annotations.comment: 摘要替换：围绕改进能否保持、迁移及其来源概述研究。

annotations.text: We organize the evidence as a diagnosis of utility, behavioral scope, and gain attribution. Standard-task evaluations of SkillEvolver, SPARK, and CoEvoSkills first establish the observed utility of completed artifacts across two runs. Controlled task changes then reveal different scopes of usefulness, and artifact and trace inspection examines the decisions preserved during reuse. This motivates the next diagnostic step: locating an improvement in the artifact's evolution history. Complementary studies of SkillRevise, SkillHone, and SkillOpt use retention tests and lifecycle interventions to examine trace-conditioned revision, history-based iterative honing, and validation-gated editing. Each study addresses a specific part of the identification question.

annotations.text: Diagnosing the Scope of Skill Utility The first diagnostic question is where a completed skill is useful. A positive source-task result can arise from content that applies across instances or from a procedure fitted to the original task. We distinguish these possibilities by first exam- ining paired utility in two standard-task runs, then deploying frozen skills under three forms of task variation. Inspection of skill content and execution traces connects the resulting utility profiles to decisions made during deployment.

annotations.text: Experimental Setup We evaluate SkillEvolver (Zhang et al. 2026a), SPARK (Zhou et al. 2026b), and CoEvoSkills (Zhang et al. 2026b) on SkillsBench (Li et al. 2026), with two runs per method. Each run pairs an execution using the generated or evolved skill with a no-skill execution of the same task. Both runs of each method use the same task set: 81 tasks for SkillEvolver, 84 for SPARK, and 85 for CoEvoSkills. annotations.text: Source-Task Gains Recur across Runs All three methods have positive mean paired gains in both runs (Table 1). SkillEvolver gains 25.61 and 25.02 points, CoEvoSkills gains 10.24 and 9.76, and SPARK gains 1.84 and 6.45. SkillEvolver and CoEvoSkills retain similar gains despite substantial changes in their no-skill scores. Their benefit is therefore more consistent across runs than their absolute skill-condition scores suggest. The task-level results also differ. SkillEvolver has at least four times as many improvements as regressions in each run; CoEvoSkills improves 17 tasks in each run, with nine and ten regressions. SPARK’s first run is nearly balanced, while its second has 13 improvements and five regressions. These results establish recurring source-task utility. We next ask whether the same frozen skills remain useful after the task changes.

annotations.text: Task Changes Separate Different Scopes of Utility We apply each source-task skill to controlled variants with- out further evolution. Input-representation changes (P1) al- ter names, column arrangements, or schemas; task-instance changes (P2) replace the data or instance structure; coupled- requirement changes (P3) alter or add requirements that must be satisfied together. These variations test whether a frozen skill remains useful when the executor must reinterpret in- puts, recompute a solution, or accommodate new require- ments. The complete record contains 222 variants and 886 condition-level results across no skill and the three meth- ods. Table 2 summarizes historical and recovery evaluations for 222 SkillEvolver variants and 221 each for SPARK and CoEvoSkills, pairing each skill condition with the no-skill result on the same variant.
annotations.comment: 新增实验：标准任务与变体结果、技能复用实例，以及基于两篇方法论文的反馈机制解释。

annotations.text: Source-task improvement does not imply useful gener- alization. All three methods improve mean reward on the source tasks in both runs, but their variant results diverge. SkillEvolver retains a positive mean gain of 11.94 points, SPARK is close to neutral at +0.65, and CoEvoSkills falls below the no-skill baseline at −5.01. SkillEvolver also im- proves more variants than it regresses (47 versus 20), whereas SPARK and CoEvoSkills show the reverse. Thus, the source- task gains of the latter two methods do not translate into a consistent advantage on changed tasks.

annotations.text: What the Evolved Skills Preserve Successful skills retain guidance for choosing and check- ing. In exoplanet detection, the SkillEvolver skill supports successful detection after input columns are rearranged (P1) and after the task requires two signals (P3). The CoEvoSkills skill fails both variants: its use leads to stellar modulation being reported as the target signal, and a signal and its har- monic being treated as two separate signals. The SkillEvolver skill explicitly organizes candidate discovery, signal diagno- sis, and refinement, including checks for misleading peaks. This case suggests that preserving criteria for accepting a result can be more useful under task changes than retaining a search routine alone. Both skills fail the replacement-instance P2 variant, so the successful checks address only part of this task family’s variation. A similar distinction appears in scheduling. The SkillE- volver and SPARK skills succeed on all three variants; the CoEvoSkills skill succeeds only on P3. In P1, using the Co- EvoSkills skill yields an otherwise valid schedule that fails the requirement to place each operation at its earliest feasible

annotations.text: The feedback used to build a skill helps explain its con- tents. The two methods differ in how they turn experi- ence into revisions. SkillEvolver compares successful and failed deployments of a candidate skill, then patches guid- ance that was missing or misleading. Its independent audit also checks for relianceontraining-instanceconstants(Zhang et al. 2026a). These mechanisms directly target both omit- ted conditions and instance-specific assumptions. The rules retained in our scheduling and signal-detection skills are con- sistent with that emphasis: they describe what to check when reusing a procedure. CoEvoSkills obtains detailed revision feedback from a co- evolving surrogate verifier; the ground-truth oracle returns only an opaque pass/fail signal (Zhang et al. 2026b). Con- sequently, discovering an omitted condition depends on the surrogate reconstructing it from the task and observed out- puts. This offers a plausible explanation for a skill that covers many feasibility checks but misses a condition needed for successful reuse, as in the scheduling example. Both meth- ods generate reusable skill packages; the relevant difference is which failure information becomes persistent guidance. Our interpretation is that feedback coverage and abstraction from the source instance help determine the scope of the resulting skill.

annotations.text: Connecting utility to the evolution process. The results identify useful skills and differences in their applicability; the examples suggest how retained guidance relates to those differences. The next studies test where improvements enter the lifecycle, using parent-to-final comparisons and interven- tions on feedback, selection, skill content, and verification in SkillRevise, SkillHone, and SkillOpt.

annotations.text: We diagnose where the gains from self-evolving persistent skills reside and how far they extend. All three methods in the standard-task evaluations have positive paired gains in both runs, but task variation separates their utility profiles. SkillEvolver remains positive across representation, instance, and requirement changes; SPARK combines gains on two probes with a decline on instance changes; CoEvoSkills declines on all three. The inspected traces identify decision criteria and correctness checks expressed during successful reuse. Complementary lifecycle interventions show that adopted artifact components can change behavior, selected outcomes can disappear under fresh deployment, and fixed outputs can receive different verdicts under different verifiers. Together, these findings distinguish useful artifacts, their behavioral scope, and the processes that produce or measure their apparent improvement.
annotations.comment: 结论重写：总结收益存在、范围分化、行为决策与生命周期机制的诊断关系。
